courts.headline: Braintree driver banned after roof load smashed into armed police car on A120
courts.summary: A panel flew off his Audi near Stansted Airport, crossed the central barrier and shattered a police car's windscreen.
body: A Braintree driver whose unsecured roof load smashed into an Essex Police armed response car on the A120 near Stansted Airport has been banned from driving for a year. The panel flew off his Audi, cleared the central barrier and shattered the police car's windscreen, showering both officers with glass.

Glen Lillie, 34, of Park Drive, Braintree, pleaded guilty to three charges and was given a 12-month community order with 140 hours of unpaid work at Colchester Magistrates' Court on 22 October. The collision happened at about 1.30pm on 19 December 2025 near Little Canfield as officers drove to an emergency on blue lights. Lillie did not stop or report it, but police traced him through images of a car carrying a large flat item on a roof rack.

Police said the officer brought the damaged Volvo to a controlled stop, and the dual carriageway was closed while debris was cleared. The car was off the road for several months. PC Simon Bailey said the outcome could have been devastating and urged drivers to secure their loads.

official.headline: Medieval Southchurch Hall shuts until mid-2027 for £423,000 conservation work
official.summary: The Grade I listed moated manor house in Southend has closed to visitors while its roof, windows and stonework are repaired.
body: Southchurch Hall, the Grade I listed medieval manor house in Southend, closed to visitors on 1 November for a major conservation project. Southend-on-Sea City Council says the building is expected to stay shut until around the middle of 2027 while the work is carried out.

The £423,105 programme is funded by Arts Council England's Museums Estate and Development Fund and covers repairs to the roof and windows, conservation of the masonry, better drainage and refurbished visitor toilets. The moated hall dates from the mid-14th century and stands on the site of an earlier Saxon hall; it was a branch library from the 1930s before becoming a museum in the 1970s.

Councillor Matt Dent, cabinet member for culture, tourism and business, described the project as "once-in-a-generation conservation works" that will also improve the visitor experience. Southend Museums plans to share progress updates and behind-the-scenes stories on its social media channels while the hall is closed.
points: Closed to visitors from 1 November 2026
Reopening provisionally mid-2027

stories.headline: Racing returns to Chelmsford City, but Ladbrokes and Coral refuse to take bets
stories.summary: The Great Leighs track staged its first meeting since March under new operator Arc, with a betting row hanging over the comeback.
body: Horse racing returned to Chelmsford City Racecourse on Monday evening for the first time since March, with Arena Racing Company (Arc) now running the track. The comeback was overshadowed by a commercial dispute, as Ladbrokes and Coral offered no betting or pictures on the eight-race card, the Racing Post reports.

Entain, which owns both bookmakers, said it is in talks with Arc and will not show Chelmsford fixtures in its shops or online until those talks conclude, leaving about 2,300 betting shops without live pictures. Arc said it looked forward to continuing positive discussions. TV coverage of the course has moved from Racing TV to Sky Sports Racing.

Racing stopped after the former licence holder, Great Leighs Estates, went into administration and the BHA blocked another company from taking over. Arc agreed a lease at the start of October and the BHA gave final approval on 23 October. The next meetings are on 5 and 26 November, followed by 3, 10 and 17 December.

stories.headline: Walsall pledge support for Colchester keeper after alleged racist remark

points: The incident is said to have happened during Saturday's League Two fixture

body: Walsall have said they will support Colchester United goalkeeper Thimothee Lo-Tutala after a fan reportedly made a racist comment during Saturday's League Two match between the sides. A report of discriminatory language directed at a Colchester player is now being investigated by the relevant authorities.

Walsall won the game 3-1. In a joint statement, the two clubs said "discrimination of any kind will not be tolerated" and that no one, in football or wider society, should have to face it. Anyone found responsible could face arrest or a football banning order.

No details have been given of who made the report or what action has been taken so far, and the investigation is continuing. Walsall's offer of support for Lo-Tutala sits alongside the clubs' joint condemnation of the alleged abuse.

stories.summary: Colchester United lost 3-1 to Walsall in League Two, their first home league defeat of the campaign.
body: Colchester United suffered their first home league defeat of the League Two season on Saturday, beaten 3-1 by Walsall at the JobServe Community Stadium. The visitors were ahead inside three minutes and pulled away late on.

Declan Skura scored from close range after a corner in the third minute. Colchester thought Sean Raggett had headed an equaliser, but it was ruled out for a foul in the build-up, before Jack Payne levelled from the penalty spot in the 35th minute after Moses Sesay was fouled. Walsall keeper Jed Ward made several saves, Pressley headed the visitors back in front from Mason Hancock's cross in the 79th minute, and Clarke added a third in stoppage time.

The result ended Colchester's unbeaten home league record for the campaign. Walsall's supporters' site Bescot Banter described a much-improved second half from the visitors, who were more clinical in front of goal.

stories.summary: Southend United led twice in Ruislip through Leon Chambers-Parillon, only for Wealdstone to fight back and snatch a stoppage-time winner.
body: Southend United were beaten 3-2 by Wealdstone in the National League on Saturday after Olufela Olomola scored deep into stoppage time. It was a painful afternoon for the Shrimpers, who twice held the lead in Ruislip but left with nothing.

Leon Chambers-Parillon put Southend ahead inside five minutes when the ball broke loose in the box, but Fejiri Okenabirhie levelled from the spot on 24 minutes after Dylan Kadji was fouled. Chambers-Parillon restored the advantage with a strike from outside the area on 39 minutes. Luke Norris headed Wealdstone level just after the hour before Olomola settled it in the 94th minute.

Kieron Dyer's side went into the game third in the table on 29 points from 16 matches, with Boreham Wood top on 44. Wealdstone started the day 18th on 18 points, so the defeat was a setback for Southend's push near the top of the division.

body: Chelmsford City won 3-1 away at AFC Totton in the Enterprise National League South on Saturday 31 October. The result followed a 1-0 victory at Dover Athletic earlier in the week, giving the Clarets back-to-back league wins.

Mark Cooper's side travelled to the Snows Stadium unbeaten in 12 league matches, with Harry Barbrook's 42nd-minute goal having settled the game at Dover. Defender Nathan Ralph said before the trip: "We're feeling positive as a group and feel like we're in a good place." Totton, managed by Scott Rendell, had won 2-1 when the sides met in Hampshire in October 2025.
Totton started the afternoon 17th in the table with 16 points from 14 games. The club says Chelmsford now face a busy run of fixtures in November.

body: ACA Harlow, the town's Advanced Cricket Academy, has agreed a two-year sponsorship deal with Essex Cricket covering the 2027 and 2028 seasons. As part of the partnership, a stand at the Graham Gooch End of Chelmsford's Ambassador Cruise Line Ground will be named the ACA Harlow stand.

The indoor centre, owned by John Sullivan, opened in 2025 and has six batting lanes, bowling machines and AI analysis software, with coaches qualified up to ECB Level 4. It already gives Essex County Age Group pathway squads free use of its facilities and took pitch-side advertising at Chelmsford in 2026. Sullivan said the deal would let customers learn from players at the top of the county game, while Essex's head of business operations, Lorraine Fletcher, said it would open up development opportunities for players across the county.

Over the next two seasons the package will bring master-class sessions at ACA Harlow with Essex men's and women's professionals, ticket offers for ACA customers and a presence at the county's mini-match-play event. The academy's branding will also appear on the Chelmsford scoreboard and on live streams of domestic matches.

body: Chelmsford Chieftains beat Cardiff Fire 7-2 at Riverside Ice and Leisure on Saturday 31 October to stay top of NIHL South Division 1. The win was their fifth of the league campaign and kept them clear of their nearest challengers.

Kieran Raynor scored in the first period before the Chieftains took control in the second period, when Rio Grinell-Parke, Lane Paddison, Callum Wells and Ollie Baldock all found the net. Baldock added a second in the final period and Tom Soar completed the scoring, while Owen and Rhys Smetham replied for Cardiff. Hallden Barnes-Garner had four assists, and goaltender Brandon Stones was named man of the match after facing 25 shots as the hosts fired 47 at Morgan Parsons.
The Chieftains have 21 points from eight games, five ahead of both Slough Jets and Streatham Redhawks, who each have games in hand. This was game eight of a 27-match league season.

stories.headline: Henry Nowak's family to tell their fight for justice in ITV documentary on Thursday night
stories.summary: The Home Secretary says she has full confidence in the police watchdog, whose inquiry into two officers is due to end early next year before Alex Chalk examines its own role.
body: The family of Henry Nowak, the 18-year-old former Harris Academy Chafford Hundred pupil stabbed to death in Southampton in December 2025, have accused some politicians of exploiting his murder. His mother, Lucy Ross, said she was not interested in their "political game", and the family said Henry would have hated the riots that followed his death.

Henry was stabbed five times as he walked home from a night out by Vickrum Digwa, who falsely claimed Henry had racially abused him and has since been jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years. Officers handcuffed Henry as he lay dying, and his stepmother Katie Nowak said the family had been failed "multiple times". Hampshire and Isle of Wight's chief constable has apologised, saying officers failed Henry when he most needed help.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct is investigating two officers for potential gross misconduct, and Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has asked former lord chancellor Alex Chalk to lead an independent review of missed chances to intervene. Speaking to ITV News on Tuesday, Ms Mahmood said she still had full confidence in the watchdog despite criticism of its handling of the case, and Mr Chalk's review will look at the IOPC's own actions once its investigation ends, expected early next year. The family tell their story in the ITV Tonight special Dear Henry: Our Fight for Justice, on ITV1 at 9pm on Thursday 5 November.

stories.headline: Maldon car parks go cashless and paperless as 12 new pay machines arrive
stories.summary: Contactless-only machines with no paper tickets are being fitted in the town centre and Promenade Park, with work due to finish by 20 November.
body: Drivers in Maldon will no longer be able to pay for council parking with cash or get a paper ticket, as Maldon District Council replaces its machines this month. Twelve new contactless-only machines are going in across the town centre and Promenade Park, where drivers will type in their registration number and can ask for an email receipt.

The machines are being fitted at White Horse Lane, Butt Lane, High Street East, Friary Fields and the Promenade Park visitor car parks, with five running on solar power. Nine little-used machines will be removed, and the Council Offices car park and Promenade Park coach park will take RingGo payments only. The council says RingGo, used since 2018, now accounts for 63% of sessions at Promenade Park and 30% in the town centre.

The work is due to be finished by 20 November, and RingGo stays available wherever it is used now. Council leader Simon Morgan said going paperless would cut waste, and the council says it will lower running and maintenance costs. Signs are going up in car parks and answers to common questions are on the council website.

Thurrock Nub News reported that the arrest was made in Clarence Road, near the Barclays branch, in one of the busiest parts of the town.

Martin Heward, of Palmers Avenue, Grays, is charged with possession of an imitation firearm with intent to cause fear of violence and with racially aggravated harassment. Witnesses had told Thurrock Nub News that officers were heard shouting at a man to put a gun down, and that another man was briefly handcuffed and then released before the arrest.

Mr Heward was remanded in custody and was due before Basildon Magistrates' Court on Tuesday 3 November. Police thanked everyone who spoke to officers and helped with their enquiries after the incident.

body: Brentwood Borough Council has approved plans by Vistry Group for 182 homes on land near Doddinghurst Road, on the edge of Brentwood close to Pilgrims Hatch. The site is already allocated for around 200 homes in the borough's plans.

The scheme mixes flats with houses of up to four bedrooms, with 64 affordable homes and 118 for private sale, alongside open space, a play area and seating. The council received 97 objections about traffic, infrastructure and flooding, and one resident warned there are no official crossing points for children walking to local schools.

Council officers concluded that the objections did not outweigh the benefit of delivering new homes on an allocated site. Peter Willis, managing director of Vistry Eastern Home Counties, called the approval a "significant step forward" for local housing needs.

body: Councils across Greater Essex say residents should notice no difference in their day-to-day services while the government reviews its plans to reorganise local government in the county. The previous decision, which would have replaced the current councils with five new unitary authorities, was withdrawn in September and a final ruling is now not expected until early 2027.

The government announced a review of its reorganisation programme on 7 September 2026 and pulled its Greater Essex decision while that work takes place. The withdrawn plan, announced in March, would have merged Thurrock and Basildon into a South West Essex Council. Thurrock Council says existing councils will keep operating as normal and that there are "no changes to how residents access Thurrock Council services".

Southend-on-Sea City Council says ministers will make their decision by early 2027, and its leader, Councillor Daniel Cowan, says the city will keep arguing for a five-unitary model. Epping Forest District Council says the government has confirmed that elections in May 2027 will go ahead on existing boundaries. Under the old timetable, Thurrock Council would have closed on 31 March 2028, but the review means those dates are now uncertain.

stories.summary: A young chef who spent four months critically ill after being hit by a speeding driver in Witham is sharing his recovery to warn other young drivers.
body: A 21-year-old chef from Witham who was left critically ill after being hit by a speeding driver is telling his story to help persuade young drivers in Essex to slow down. Fletcher Rice is the face of No Respawns, a Safer Essex Roads Partnership campaign that uses the language of video games to show that real roads offer no second chances.

Mr Rice was on a pedestrian crossing at Chipping Hill on 17 August 2025 when he was struck by a car travelling at 53mph in a 30mph zone on the wrong side of the road. He had just qualified as a chef and spent four months in a critical condition with serious head injuries and fractures to his pelvis, shoulder, collarbone, arm and finger. The driver, Conner Phillips, 22, of Mann Close, Witham, admitted dangerous driving and causing serious injury by dangerous driving and was jailed for two years in June.

Mr Rice still struggles to walk, run and play the guitar, and said: "Now my life's been put on hold." Adam Pipe of Essex Police praised his determination and said the driver's selfishness had left him facing extensive rehabilitation. Campaign manager William Cubbin said young people often underestimate the dangers of speeding because they feel invulnerable behind the wheel.

stories.summary: Police seized four dogs and four vehicles after reports of hare coursing on the Dengie marshes on Wednesday morning.
body: Five men have been reported for hare coursing, and four dogs and four vehicles seized, after a police operation on the Dengie marshes. Officers were called at about 8am on Wednesday 28 October following several reports from the public.

Essex Police's Rural Engagement Team, local officers, the Dog Section and the National Police Air Service helicopter took part. The men, in their 20s and 30s and from Basildon, Cambridgeshire, London and Northamptonshire, were reported for offences under the Hunting Act 2004 and each given a three-year community protection warning, and three more people are due to be interviewed.

Inspector Terry Jacobs said hare coursing can devastate rural communities, damaging land and crops and putting wildlife at risk. Police ask anyone who sees it happening to call 999 with a What3Words location, descriptions and vehicle registrations, and to report other rural crime online, through Live Chat or on 101.

stories.headline: Thurrock adopts new flag policy, ending Pride and Ukraine flags at civic offices
points: The borough coat of arms, Union Flag and St George's Flag will fly at the Civic Offices in Grays
Tilbury Civic Square will fly the Canadian Flag too, recalling Canadian troops stationed there in the First World War
Leader Richard Bingley says the policy is about civic pride
The policy also sets a process for marking civic occasions and commemorations
stories.summary: Thurrock's Reform-led council has set out which flags will fly at its Grays offices and in Tilbury, and the Pride and Ukrainian flags are no longer allowed.
body: Thurrock Council has adopted a new flag-flying policy that sets out which flags fly at its civic buildings, meaning the Pride and Ukrainian flags will no longer be raised outside the Civic Offices in Grays. The Reform-led administration announced the change shortly before the Remembrance season.

Under the policy the Civic Offices will fly the Thurrock coat of arms, the Union Flag and the St George's Flag, while Tilbury's Civic Square will fly the Union Flag, the St George's Flag and the Canadian flag, marking the borough's links with Canadian troops stationed in Tilbury during the First World War. Council leader Richard Bingley said flags are "more than symbols on a pole".

The council says the policy is part of its civic pride campaign and gives a clear framework for marking civic occasions and commemorations through the year. After taking control in May, Reform had already said it would lower the Ukrainian flag that had flown since the war escalated, and declined to fly the Pride flag during the borough's Pride Week.

points: A GB Railfreight container train partially derailed at Barking on 23 October
About 1.2km of track must be replaced, along with signalling and cabling

Passengers from Dagenham Dock, Rainham, Purfleet and Grays are asked not to travel
stories.summary: Trains are still not stopping at Purfleet, Rainham or Dagenham Dock after a freight derailment near Barking, and c2c's operator says the disruption will last until at least the week of 9 November.
body: c2c passengers in south Essex face more disruption this week, with trains still not calling at Purfleet, Rainham or Dagenham Dock after a freight train came off the tracks near Barking. GBR Anglia, which runs c2c, says repairs will go on until at least the week beginning 9 November and is asking people travelling from Dagenham Dock, Rainham, Purfleet and Grays not to travel.

A GB Railfreight container train from London Gateway partially derailed at Barking at about 1.10pm on Friday 23 October, and no injuries were reported. Around 1.2km of track needs replacing, along with damaged signalling equipment and cabling, and some sections must be rebuilt entirely. Rob Mullen, chief customer and commercial director at GBR Anglia, apologised in a video and said much of the infrastructure "must be completely rebuilt".

Rail replacement buses are running between Upminster and Grays, calling at Rainham and Purfleet, and c2c tickets are valid at no extra cost on Greater Anglia trains, some TfL buses and buses between Purfleet and Grays. Passengers using Dagenham Dock are advised to take a local bus to Dagenham Heathway or Barking. Delayed passengers may be able to claim Delay Repay compensation, and c2c says timescales could still change.

stories.headline: Police inquiries go on into three suspicious items found at Brentwood home as couple face threats-to-kill charges
points: Items found at a Sawyers Grove address on Friday 30 October
Thomas Walker, 43, and Yolanda-Tony King, 48, both charged with making threats to kill
Pair were listed before Basildon magistrates on Monday
Police say inquiries into the suspicious items remain ongoing
stories.summary: Essex Police say their investigation into the items found during Friday's bomb disposal operation in Sawyers Grove is continuing, after a man and a woman were charged.
body: A man and a woman have been charged after three small homemade explosive devices were found at a house in Sawyers Grove, Brentwood, on Friday. The discovery led police to set up a 100-metre cordon and evacuate about 40 nearby properties while bomb disposal experts dealt with the items.

Thomas Walker, 43, is charged with three counts of criminal damage and making threats to kill, and Yolanda-Tony King, 48, with two counts of criminal damage, harassment and making threats to kill, Greatest Hits Radio reports. Both live in Sawyers Grove and were due before magistrates in Basildon on Monday 2 November. Officers had forced entry to the address at about 7.20am on Friday after reports of a disturbance.

Essex Police said inquiries into the suspicious items recovered from the address were continuing. Residents who had to leave their homes were given shelter at the King George's Playing Fields pavilion, and the cordon has since been lifted.

stories.headline: Essex gets third-largest share of new GP domestic abuse fund, with £950,000 in year one
stories.summary: Patients in Southend, Essex and Thurrock will be able to raise domestic abuse or sexual violence with their GP practice and be linked to specialist help, under a three-year national pilot.
points: NHS Essex's award totals £4,454,124 over three years
Year one is worth £949,525, rising to £1,769,524 in 2027/28
Only two first-wave bids received more money than Essex
Patients are referred on only if they agree

also.name: GOV.UK (Department of Health and Social Care)

body: Victims of domestic abuse and sexual violence in Essex are to get extra help through their GP surgeries after NHS Essex won more than £4.4 million from the national Steps to Safety programme. The money covers Southend, Essex and Thurrock, making the county one of the first places in England to introduce the scheme.

Government figures show the Essex award is worth £4,454,124 over three years, starting with £949,525 in 2026/27 and rising to £1,769,524 in 2027/28 and £1,735,075 in 2028/29. That is the third largest of the 12 first-phase awards, behind a joint Coventry and Warwickshire bid with Herefordshire and Worcestershire, and North East and North Cumbria. The funding will pay for a specialist provider, training for practice staff and support workers attached to groups of surgeries, who will act as a single point of contact for patients referred with their consent. William Guy, NHS Essex's director of commissioning for primary care and neighbourhoods, said practice teams "build trusted relationships with patients over many years".

NHS Essex says it will spend the coming months drawing up plans with GP practices, specialist abuse services and local partners, and has not yet confirmed a timetable. Nationally, the first phase is worth up to £34.4 million over three years, with the scheme being rolled out in three phases from April 2026 and due to reach the whole of England by 2029. An independent evaluation will look at how it works and what difference it makes.

stories.headline: Harlow Council tells owners of badly neglected gardens to clear up or face action
stories.summary: Rubbish heaps and overgrowth are in the council's sights, with inspections of a first group of homes due within days.
points: Inspections of the first properties take place over the coming week
Private owners face Section 215 notices if they refuse to act
Ignoring a notice can lead to prosecution or a council clear-up charged to the owner
Council tenants will be held to their tenancy agreements
body: Harlow Council has launched an enforcement drive against severely neglected front and back gardens, warning those responsible to clear them or face action. The council says piles of rubbish, heavy overgrowth and long-term neglect draw in vermin and cause problems for neighbouring homes.

A first set of properties has been identified and will be inspected over the following week so the worst cases can be dealt with first. Where privately owned gardens are not put right, the council plans to issue Section 215 notices if the legal tests are met, and owners who ignore them could be prosecuted or have the work done by the council and the cost recovered from them. Council leader Dan Swords said of neglectful owners: "Their neglect becomes your problem."

Council tenants are required to look after their gardens under their tenancy agreements, and the council says it will enforce those terms where they are broken. Councillor Hardware, cabinet member for planning, said each case would have a set course of action with clear requirements and deadlines. The programme forms part of the council's zero tolerance approach to enforcement under its Building Harlow's Future plans.

stories.headline: 237 extra escalation beds ready for winter across Essex hospitals, 113 of them at Harlow's PAH
stories.summary: Harlow's Princess Alexandra Hospital holds nearly half of the county's extra winter beds, as the NHS braces for longer A&E waits and ambulance delays.
points: 2,724 core acute beds plus 237 for use under pressure
PAH: 447 core and 113 escalation beds
Mid and South Essex trust has 1,652 core beds and 51 escalation beds
426 community places aim to keep people out of hospital
body: Nearly 3,000 acute hospital beds will be available across Essex this winter, according to NHS Essex, including 237 escalation beds that can be opened when hospitals are under extra strain. Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow accounts for 113 of those extra beds, the largest share of any hospital in the county.

Of the 2,961 beds in total, 2,724 are core beds: 1,652 across the Mid and South Essex trust, 625 at Colchester Hospital and 447 at PAH. Colchester has a further 73 escalation beds and Mid and South Essex 51. On top of this, 426 places are available through intermediate care, virtual wards, hospital at home and urgent community response teams, aimed at keeping patients out of acute wards and helping them home sooner.

The integrated care board said its winter work was about making sure the capacity "is utilised to best effect". It has been asked to explain why its figures list 340 adult and older adult mental health beds when overall capacity is reported as 430, and whether the escalation beds are extra compared with last winter. Health leaders warn that illness, staff absence, outbreaks, bad weather and delayed discharges can all squeeze beds, leading to longer A&E waits and ambulance handover delays.

stories.headline: Basildon councillors set their stance on 910 Foots Farm homes at Billericay tonight
stories.summary: Officers back the green belt scheme south of Billericay, but with an appeal already lodged, a government inspector will make the final call.
body: Basildon councillors meet on Tuesday 3 November to decide the council's position on plans for up to 910 homes on farmland at Foots Farm, south of Billericay. The developers have already appealed to the government because the council missed its deadline to decide, so the vote will shape the council's case at a public inquiry rather than grant or refuse permission.

The 56.89-hectare green belt site lies between Coxes Farm Road and the A129 Southend Road, next to Great Burstead and South Green. Half the homes would be affordable, alongside eight Gypsy and Traveller pitches, a community hub, a nursery and primary school site and around 23 hectares of green space. Officers accept the scheme is inappropriate green belt development but say the harm is outweighed, citing a housing land supply of just over two years.

The council received 225 objections, and Great Burstead and South Green Parish Council is strongly opposed, with residents worried about schools, GPs, roads and flooding. The NHS says local surgeries already lack space. The same meeting will confirm the formal reason for refusing 175 homes at Tye Common Road, which councillors voted against in October.

stories.headline: Westgate shoppers in Basildon to get 90 minutes' free parking from December
stories.summary: Basildon Council has hired a new operator for its Westgate car parks, with cameras to deter long stays and a free short-stay period for shoppers.
body: Drivers using Westgate Shopping Park in Basildon are set to get 90 minutes of free parking from December, under a new contract agreed by Basildon Council. The council says the change should make it easier to visit the town centre and support its shops and leisure venues.

Sagoss Ltd has been appointed to run parking at Westgate after a tender, and number plate recognition cameras will be used to enforce the rules and cut unauthorised and long-stay parking. The council owns the shopping park, where Aldi is due to open on 12 November. Current charges run from £1.55 for two hours in the multi-storey to 75p all day on Sundays.

The new system is expected to start in December once the contract and set-up are complete, but no exact date has been given. The decision record does not yet say which car parks the free period covers or how overstays will be charged, so drivers should keep paying as normal until signs go up.

stories.headline: Essex agrees plan to cap daily school bus fares for pupils
stories.summary: County Hall has backed a package aimed at bringing down the cost of getting to school by bus, including talks with operators.
body: Essex County Council has approved plans to bring down the cost of school bus travel, including a cap on daily fares for students. The move matters to thousands of families across the county who rely on buses to get children to school.

The package also includes opening negotiations with bus operators over student fares and seeking to commission more school bus services directly. The council says it will look at running services itself where they could offer better value, and will consider options for transport for young people aged 16 and over with special educational needs and disabilities.

The Reform UK-run council has not yet set out the level of the cap or when it will take effect, according to the trade publication Local Transport Today. Further details are expected as talks with operators get under way.

stories.headline: Fewer than one in ten Essex adults now smoke, the lowest share on record
stories.summary: The proportion of adults who smoke in Essex has dropped from 11% to 9.2%, the county council says, as it pushes towards a smoke-free county by 2030.
body: The share of adults in Essex who smoke has fallen to 9.2%, down from 11%, according to the latest three-year figures, the lowest level on record. Essex County Council says stop-smoking services across the county are helping people quit, though rates remain higher in some of the most deprived communities.

Help is offered through the Essex Wellbeing Service, which provides free stop-smoking aids, advice on newer medicines where suitable and one-to-one coaching to help people deal with triggers during a quit attempt. Smokers can also get free access to the online Allen Carr Easyway course. Councillor Chris Hossack, cabinet member for residents and community services, called the figures promising.

The county has set itself the goal of becoming smoke-free by 2030. Cllr Hossack said more work was needed where smoking remains most common and that the council would keep working with partners so people can get support to stop for good.

stories.headline: Essex Libraries begin a year of centenary events with exhibitions in four towns
stories.summary: Displays, story times and a countywide reading list mark 100 years since the county library service was set up in 1926.
body: Essex Libraries have started a programme of events to mark a century since the county library service was formally set up. Activities begin this month and run through the autumn in libraries across Essex, under the theme of supporting the people of the county.

The first County Library Committee met in May 1926, the first County Librarian was appointed that July and the first headquarters opened in January 1927. Basildon, Chelmsford, Colchester and Harlow libraries will host flagship exhibitions on their local history, while branches across the county stage displays of historic photographs and readers' memories under the banner 100 Years, 100 Books, 100 Stories.

Children's story times, trails and crafts themed on different decades are planned, along with a new countywide reading list, reading challenges on the Read On app and a touring Agatha Christie exhibition. Essex County Council cabinet member Chris Hossack said libraries had been at the heart of communities for 100 years.

stories.headline: Minister warns Basildon that pulling its 29,000-home local plan could be unlawful
stories.summary: Housing minister Matthew Pennycook has written to the council leader after councillors voted to withdraw the plan as a last resort if their legal challenge fails.
body: Housing minister Matthew Pennycook has warned Basildon Borough Council that withdrawing its draft local plan, which allows for about 29,000 homes, could be unlawful, Inside Housing reports. The borough's plan has not been updated for 27 years, and the row decides how much green belt land could be built on across Basildon, Billericay and Wickford.

At an extraordinary meeting on 26 October, councillors backed a motion from Reform UK mayor Sam Journet to withdraw the plan from progressing beyond the Regulation 19 stage, but only if the council's planned judicial review of government intervention fails. Mr Pennycook wrote to council leader Andy Barnes the same day saying his July direction bars any step towards withdrawal and that he could take over the plan. Labour councillors refused to take part in the vote, with Gavin Callaghan calling the motion irresponsible.

The council will also write to the government objecting to housing targets it says put pressure on the green belt without matching infrastructure. Ministers say the directions remain in force and that the government will step in if councils fail to put up-to-date plans in place, though Mr Pennycook has said he will consider Basildon's request for more time.

stories.headline: Harlow MP raises Poundland's two shops and depot in the Commons as chain's future hangs in the balance
stories.summary: Chris Vince asked ministers what they are doing about the discount retailer, which has two stores and a depot in the town.
body: Harlow MP Chris Vince has raised fears for Poundland's future in the House of Commons, pointing out that the retailer has two shops and a depot in his constituency, Your Harlow reports. He described the business as hugely important to the town.

Mr Vince welcomed the Chancellor's recent announcement on support for high streets, then asked what conversations ministers had held with Cabinet colleagues about Poundland. Minister Jim McMahon replied that everyone was concerned about the announcement affecting Poundland and its 30,000 staff.

Mr McMahon said the government was in talks with Poundland to support it where it could, and acknowledged the impact on communities such as Harlow. Your Harlow reported last week that the chain's future was in the balance.

stories.headline: Remembrance poppies painted on roads in 12 Essex towns, from Dunmow to Clacton
stories.summary: Essex County Council is marking Remembrance with poppy emblems on the road surface in a dozen places, and says it is also spending on the upkeep of war memorials.
body: Essex County Council is painting Remembrance poppies on roads in 12 towns across the county as a tribute to those who died in service and those who served. The emblems will be seen by drivers, cyclists and pedestrians in the run-up to Remembrance Sunday.

The locations are Dunmow High Street, Harlow, Brentwood, Hadleigh, Pitsea, Epping, Braintree, Rochford, Chelmsford, Maldon, Clacton and Colchester. Council leader Peter Harris said the poppies would be a "powerful visual tribute", while highways cabinet member Mark Webster, himself a veteran, said it mattered to keep honouring those who died serving the country.

The council says it is also investing in refurbishing and maintaining war memorials so they stay fitting places for reflection. Its armed forces champion, Terry Longstaff, said the emblems showed the county's commitment to preserving the legacy of those who served.
